newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel eases West Bank sanctions.
newsitem.headline: Israel eases West Bank sanctions.

text.p: The Israeli army said on Thursday it had lifted its siege of the Palestinian West Bank towns of Hebron and Ramallah but the town of Bethlehem and an area surrounding Jerusalem remained sealed off.
"From this morning the internal closure was lifted from Hebron and Ramallah," an army spokeswoman said.
The spokeswoman emphasised the general ban against Palestinians from the West Bank and the Gaza Strip entering Israel remained in place.

Israel sealed off the West Bank and Gaza Strip and restricted Palestinians in the West Bank to their towns and villages after a July 30 twin suicide bombing at an Israeli market killed 16 people, including the two attackers.

The bombing plunged relations between Israel and the Palestinians to a new low. Israel suspended resumption of substantive peace talks with the Palestinians and withheld financial transfers it owed the Palestinian Authority.
Palestinians say the moves amount to collective punishment.

Israel has gradually eased the "internal closure" but the other measures remain in place. Jordan's King Hussein failed on Wednesday to persuade Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to ease the measures.
Netanyahu insisted Palestinian President Yasser Arafat had to prove he was cracking down on militants opposed to Israel-PLO peace moves before the sanctions would be lifted.
Arafat says he has fought militants. U.S. peace envoy Dennis Ross wound up a mission to the area on Wednesday saying a beginning had been made to restoring security cooperation between the sides.
U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright has said she will make her first visit to the region later this month if there is progress on security cooperation.

On Sunday, the army allowed Palestinians to travel between three besieged West Bank self-ruled cities, Jenin, Tulkarm and Qalqilya. It opened crossings linking the West Bank and Gaza with Jordan and Egypt for travel by Palestinians and others.
A siege of Jericho and Nablus was lifted on Friday. The army has given no reason for the moves.
